title: Runtime compatibility graph and deployment surface allocator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a canonical runtime compatibility representation that allows the deployment platform to decide where a given model variant can be served (hosted, dedicated, private) and to synthesize a deployment surface for canaries, A/B tests, shadowing, and staged rollouts. This ticket covers the design of a compatibility graph (nodes = environment capabilities, edges = compatibility transforms), an allocator that maps rollout intents to a concrete set of target environments, and a simulation pass that predicts safe exposure and rollback triggers before executing the rollout.
background: Current rollout tooling assumes a flat compatibility check (binary pass/fail) and duplicates environment-specific heuristics across multiple controllers. That leads to inconsistent behavior between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, surprises during canary promotion, and manual work when teams require environment-specific shims (e.g., quantization mismatch, KV cache size, kernel availability). A single compatibility graph and allocator will centralize logic and enable deterministic, testable rollout plans.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility graph schema documented and reviewed: nodes for capability (quantize-level, kernel-set, max-concurrent-seqs, tenant-isolation), edges for allowed transforms (quantize -> lower-precision, kernel-fallback), and labels for environment metadata (region, GPU-type, private/VPC constraints)
Allocator prototype that consumes a rollout intent (canary/A-B/shadow) and emits a deterministic target set of endpoints across Hosted/Dedicated/Private within latency and capacity constraints
Rollout simulation output that estimates percent-exposed, expected token-cost delta, and SLO risk score for a given plan; simulation must run in CI for canaries targeting >5% traffic
Integration tests covering three representative scenarios: hosted-only fast canary, mixed hosted+dedicated A/B with autoscale constraints, and private-only shadowing for a regulated tenant
Auto-rollback hooks integrated: simulator produces safe thresholds; controller wires thresholds and triggers rollback in staging and canary runs when exceeded
Migration guide for existing rollout configs and a compatibility-check step in the pipeline; no production changes until two-week pilot in selected orgs
tasks: Draft compatibility graph data model and JSON schema
Implement translator that maps model manifest + runtime capabilities into graph nodes
Build allocator service (stateless API) returning eligible targets and scoring by cost/latency/risk
Add rollout-simulation CLI that takes intent + sample workload and outputs risk metrics
Wire simulator into canary controller CI job and add test fixtures
Create dashboards for risk scores, target selection, and historical allocations
Run pilot with infra-team and two customer-facing teams; gather feedback
Prepare migration doc and deprecation plan for fragile environment heuristics
notes: Design should allow pluggable capability detectors so Private deployments can opt into additional checks (e.g., HSM availability, local-nfs mount). The allocator must be conservative by default to avoid routing traffic to incompatible endpoints. Consider cost-balancing policy (minimize token-cost subject to SLO) as a later flag.
